text.p: European regional carrier British Midland Airways announced on Monday a series of product improvements including the introduction of a business class to its domestic UK services.
The airline said at a trade launch here that it was extending its Diamond EuroClass to UK domestic routes from September 30 and was also introducing wider business class seats across its network.
In addition, it is opening new domestic and international business class lounges at London's Heathrow airport, and introducing self-service ticket and check-in machines there.
The new seating for business class passengers will be introduced from early next year and will effectively remove a seat from each row across the plane.
"Much recent discussion has focused on budget airlines and the so-called single "no-frills" market," said the airline's chairman Sir Michael Bishop.

"British Midland has met the challenge of these newcomers, albeit whilst offering a much higher quality product to our customers. But we also recognise there is still a market for quality service, not least in the UK," he added.
British Midland, which is 40 percent owned by Scandinavian Airlines Systems (SAS), was a single-class operator until it introduced Diamond EuroClass to its international routes in March 1993.
The airline currently operates some 35 international European and domestic UK routes and is the second largest operator at London's Heathrow airport with over 1,000 flights per week.
